transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi... well, I guess I'm here because my sleep is just... it's completely broken up now. I mean, it's a total mess. I work as a personal care aide, and I do these long overnight shifts, which, you know, they take a lot out of you physically. Usually, I can just crash the second I get home and pull the curtains shut. But lately... I get off my shift, I get in bed, and I just lie there. Wide awake. Just staring and staring for hours, feeling completely wired but exhausted at the same time. 

And then, finally, when I actually do manage to drift off for a second, it doesn't even count as sleep because I wake up just... terrified. Like, waking up suddenly and just feeling so scared, and I feel like I haven't rested a single minute. It's like I never even closed my eyes at all, just totally drained. I just... I don't know how I'm supposed to keep doing my job or taking care of people when I'm waking up like that and getting absolutely no rest. It's just not working anymore.
Do you feel panicked when you're lying awake at night?

Panicked? Um... no, not panicked, exactly. I mean, it's not like my heart is racing or I'm sweating or feeling like I'm having a heart attack or something while I'm just lying there. It's more just... this heavy, awful feeling. Like, I'm lying in the dark, and my body is so heavy, like lead, because I've been lifting people and walking on hard floors for twelve hours. But my brain is just... stuck. I wouldn't call it panic. It's just this miserable, agonizing waiting. You know? Just waiting and waiting to fall asleep, and knowing that every minute that ticks by is another minute I'm not resting. 

And I start thinking about how I have to be back at work the next night, and how I'm going to be useless if I don't sleep, but that doesn't make me panic, it just makes me feel... I don't know, hopeless? Like I'm just trapped in the bed, staring at the ceiling. The scared feeling, the real terror, that only happens *after* I finally fall asleep and wake up all of a sudden. But when I'm just lying awake? No, no panic. Just... just feeling completely empty and wired and stuck. It's so frustrating, you know? Because I know I *need* the sleep, my muscles are literally aching for it, but it just won't come.
Do you have bad dreams when you finally do fall asleep?

Bad dreams? I... I don't know. I mean, maybe? It's hard to explain because it's not like a normal nightmare where you're being chased by a monster or, you know, falling off a cliff or something that makes sense when you wake up and think about it. It's not like a movie playing in my head that I can remember the plot of. 

When I wake up feeling so terrified, it's more like... I just wake up with this overwhelming sense of dread, but I can't put my finger on exactly what I was dreaming about. It's just a feeling. A really, really bad feeling. Like something awful is right there, right in the room with me, or something terrible is about to happen, but there's no actual story to it that I can recall. 

Sometimes I try to sit there in the dark and force myself to remember if there was a face, or a voice, or a place I was in, but it's just a blank. A really scary blank. It's just that jolt, that sudden gasp for air, and my chest feeling tight, but no actual pictures in my head to explain why I'm feeling that way. So, I don't know if you'd call that a bad dream. Is it a dream if you can't remember a single thing that happened in it, just the fear it left behind? Because that's what it is. Just waking up into pure fear without any reason for it that I can point to. It makes going back to sleep impossible, because who wants to close their eyes again when that's what happens?
Is the terrified feeling you wake up with ever related to something that happened during your work shift?

Well... I mean, yes, I guess it is, but not in the way you might think. It's not like a specific, real accident that happened right in front of me, like a client falling or something that got written up in an incident report. But... it's this overwhelming feeling that I *did* do something terrible. 

Like, I'll wake up with that awful dread, gasping for air, and my mind just immediately goes straight to my clients. I have this one lady I sit with, and she's just so frail, you know? And I just... I know deep down that I missed something with her, or with one of the others. I just know it. I'll lie there and go over my shift in my head a thousand times, thinking about every time I turned them or checked their vitals. And it gets so bad that I've actually called my supervisor during the day, which I know I shouldn't do because she's busy and I'm supposed to be off the clock, but I'll beg her to look at my charts from the night before. 

And she'll look, and she always tells me the same thing. She says, you know, "Your care notes are fine, everything is perfectly documented, stop worrying." But... I just can't believe her. I don't believe her at all. Because I have this terrible, heavy knowledge, right in the absolute pit of my stomach, that one of my clients got hurt because of me. Like I forgot something crucial, or I missed a sign that they were getting sick, and now they're suffering because I wasn't paying close enough attention. 

Even when my supervisor says everything is completely fine, it just feels like... like they are just not telling me yet. You know? Like they all know I messed up, and they know someone got hurt because of my negligence, but they're just keeping it a secret from me for now. Maybe they're waiting to fire me, or waiting for the family to complain first, I don't know. But that's what that terror is. I wake up and I'm just waiting for the phone to ring, waiting for them to finally admit that I ruined someone's life because I missed something. No matter what anyone says to me, I just know I did it.
Do you think you made a mistake at work even when you're not lying in bed at night?

Yeah. Yeah, it's... it's not just at night. It's all the time. It's like this heavy, dark cloud that just follows me everywhere I go, no matter what time of day it is or what I'm doing. Even when I'm just sitting on the couch trying to drink a cup of coffee, or if I'm at the grocery store, my mind just... it just starts spinning. And it's not even just about my clients anymore, though that's a huge part of it. It's everything. 

I keep going over every little thing I've ever done wrong, you know? Like, I'll remember something I said to my mom three years ago that might have sounded sharp, or a time I couldn't help my sister with her kids because I was too tired from working, and it just crushes me. I just sit there and think about how I'm just... I'm a terrible person. I'm a worthless aide, I really am. I mean, if I was any good at my job, I wouldn't be constantly worried that I'm hurting people, right? A good aide would know they did everything right. But me? I'm just useless. 

And honestly... and this sounds crazy, but I can't shake the feeling that God is mad at me. Like, really, truly angry with me because I'm not doing enough. I'm supposed to be taking care of these vulnerable people, these frail elderly clients who can't do anything for themselves, and I'm supposed to be protecting my family, being a good daughter and sister, and I'm just failing at all of it. It feels like God is looking down at me and just seeing this completely worthless person who can't even protect the people she's supposed to. It's like a punishment, almost. This feeling. It's like I deserve to feel this awful because of how much I've messed up, even if I can't always pinpoint the exact mistake. I just know I'm failing everyone, all the time. It never stops playing in my head.
You mentioned feeling like a terrible person and a worthless aide, but do you also feel guilty about things that have nothing to do with your job?

Yeah... yeah, it's exactly like that. I mean, I know I talk about work a lot because that's where I spend so much of my time, and those people are just so vulnerable, but... it's not just work. It's really not. It's like my brain has this filing cabinet of every single mistake I've ever made in my entire life, and it just keeps pulling out the folders, one by one, and making me read them over and over. 

Like I said before, I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my family, too. It's not just the big things, it's the stupid, tiny things that probably nobody else even remembers, but I do. I remember this one time I was supposed to pick up my niece from school, and I was running like five minutes late because of traffic, and she was just standing there on the sidewalk looking confused. And I just... I can't stop thinking about that look on her face. It was years ago, but it hits me like a ton of bricks, right in my chest. I feel so incredibly guilty about it, like I abandoned her, like I proved right then and there that I can't be trusted with anything important. 

And it's my mom, too. I think about all the times I didn't call her back right away, or the times I snapped at her because I was tired after a long shift. I just sit there and replay those conversations in my head, and I feel so sick with myself. I feel like I'm just a completely worthless daughter, a worthless sister, just like I'm a worthless aide. It all bleeds together. 

And that's why... that's why I really feel like God is mad at me. Because it's not just that I'm messing up at my job, it's that I'm failing at being a decent human being to the people who are supposed to matter the most. I'm supposed to be protecting people better, you know? That's what I'm supposed to do. I'm supposed to protect my family, I'm supposed to protect my patients, and I'm just... I'm not doing it. I'm failing everyone. And I just feel this crushing guilt about all of it, all the time, from the moment I wake up until I finally manage to pass out at night. It's just a constant loop of everything I've ever done wrong, and I can't make it stop.
Do you feel guilty about things you've done in your personal relationships as much as you do about your work?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying, it's... it's just as bad, if not worse, because they all just blur together into the exact same feeling. I can't even separate work from my personal life in my head anymore. I just sit there and I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or with my family, just playing it all on a loop. 

It doesn't matter if I'm at the facility or sitting in my own living room, the guilt is just eating me alive. It just feels like I'm a completely worthless aide, and a worthless daughter, and I just can't shake this absolute certainty that God is mad at me. I mean, He has to be, right? Because He put me here to take care of people. He gave me these frail elderly clients who can't even feed themselves, and He gave me my family, and I'm just... I'm supposed to be protecting people better. That's my whole purpose. 

And instead, I just have this filing cabinet in my brain of every time I wasn't gentle enough, or every time I was too tired to help my sister, or every time I was running late. It's like I'm constantly on trial in my own head, and God is just watching me fail over and over again. I'm supposed to be a protector. I'm supposed to be the one who makes sure everyone is safe and taken care of, but I'm just so worthless at it. I can't do anything right by any of them, and I just know I'm being punished for it. It's this heavy, suffocating feeling that I've ruined everything for the people I'm supposed to love and care for, and it never, ever stops.
Do you feel like you're a bad person even when you're doing things you normally enjoy?

Enjoy? I... I don't even know if I have things I enjoy anymore, honestly. But yeah, if I even try. Like, even if I try to do something that used to make me happy, it's exactly like I was just saying. 

I used to love baking, you know? I'd make these chocolate chip cookies and bring them in for the other aides at the facility, or I'd make them for my niece. But if I try to do that now, if I even just try to stand in my kitchen and measure out the sugar or the flour, my mind just... it goes right back to it. I'll just be standing there, holding a mixing spoon, and I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or my family. It just floods in, completely ruins whatever I'm doing. 

I'll just stare at the bowl and think about how I'm just this completely worthless aide, and I shouldn't even be allowed to bake or do anything nice for myself because I don't deserve it. I mean, how can I enjoy baking or sitting down to watch a movie when I have this absolute certainty that God is mad at me? It feels like He's watching me try to have a good time, and He's just so angry because I'm not protecting people better. That's what I'm supposed to be doing, right? I'm supposed to be protecting my frail clients and taking care of my family, and instead I'm just standing there trying to make cookies while I'm failing at my one actual purpose in life. 

So, no, I can't enjoy anything. The guilt just poisons it all. I can't escape it for even five minutes to do something fun, because I just can't stop replaying every single mistake, over and over, no matter what I'm doing.
Do you feel guilty about things you've done when you're alone with no one to account to?

That's... yeah, that's actually when it's the loudest. I know I keep repeating myself about this, but it's just... it's because it's always there, especially when I'm by myself. Like, if I'm just sitting in my apartment on a Tuesday night, and the TV is off, and nobody is calling me or expecting anything from me... you'd think that would be peaceful, right? But it's not. It's so much worse. 

Because without any distractions, without anyone there to talk to, I just sit there on the edge of my bed, staring at the floorboards, and I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or my family. The silence just makes it echo. I don't need a boss or a family member standing over me to make me feel bad, because my own brain does it for them. I'll remember a time from three years ago when I forgot to bring a client their extra blanket right away, or a time I didn't listen to my sister when she was upset, and I just spiral. I'll sit there for hours, completely alone, just torturing myself with all of it.

In those quiet moments, it just hits me so hard what a completely worthless aide I am. And even if there are no people around in my apartment, I'm not really alone, because... well, because God is always watching, right? And I can just feel it weighing down on the room. I can feel that God is mad at me. He sees me sitting there by myself, knowing I'm supposed to be out there protecting people better, and He knows I'm just a total failure at it. He gave me this life to be useful and keep my vulnerable clients and my family safe, and I'm just sitting there in the dark, failing. So yeah, being alone doesn't stop the guilt at all. It just gives it more room to breathe and completely take over my mind until I'm just crying by myself with no one to even see it.
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about your mistakes, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Yeah, I mean, it's... it's impossible. It really is. I'll be trying to do something simple, like just trying to read a magazine or even just trying to focus on making a grocery list, and my brain just completely hijacks me. I'll start out thinking, okay, I need milk and bread, and then suddenly, out of nowhere, I'm thinking about Mr. Henderson from two years ago, and how he asked for a glass of water and I told him I'd be right back, but then another client fell and I got distracted, and it took me twenty minutes to get back to him. Twenty minutes. He was just sitting there, thirsty and confused, and I... I just left him. 

And once that thought starts, I can't stop it. It doesn't matter if I'm trying to figure out what kind of cereal to buy, I just keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or my family. It's like a landslide in my head. I'll try to force myself to look at the paper, to write down "eggs," but my hand won't even move because I'm so paralyzed by this overwhelming realization that I'm just a completely worthless aide. 

I'm supposed to be there for them. That's my job, that's my life. And I just fail them. And then I start thinking about my mom, and how I snapped at her last week when she called to ask how I was doing, and I just... I can't focus on anything else because the guilt is so loud. It just drowns out everything. And it's not just that I feel bad about it, it's this deep, terrifying knowledge that God is mad at me. I can feel His anger, just pressing down on me while I'm standing there in the grocery store aisle or sitting at my kitchen table. He's furious because I'm not protecting people better. He trusted me with these fragile lives, with my family, and I'm just ruining it all. So no, I can't stop thinking about it. No matter how hard I try to focus on something else, it always, always comes back to how much I've failed everyone.
Is there one particular event or action that you feel guilty about more than any other?

One particular event? I... I wish it was just one thing, honestly. If it was just one thing, maybe I could apologize or... or try to figure out how to fix it, you know? But it’s not. It’s literally everything. 

Like I’ve been trying to explain, I just keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or my family. It’s this massive, endless list playing on a loop in my head. Sure, I’ll think about the water with Mr. Henderson, or this other time I didn't sit with Mrs. Gable long enough when she was crying, or even just forgetting to call my sister back on a Sunday when she really needed to talk. But none of them stand out as the absolute worst because they all just blur together into this one huge mountain of proof that I’m just a completely worthless aide. 

A good person wouldn't have all these mistakes adding up like this. A good person would be keeping everyone safe and doing their job right. And that’s why... that’s why I just know God is mad at me. It’s not about one single sin or one specific mistake I made on a Tuesday. He’s furious because I have this whole entire history of not protecting people better. He gave me these people to look after, He put me in this position to be a caretaker, and I just ruin it every single time. So I can't pick just one event. I really can't. The guilt is for all of it, all at once, constantly pressing down on me.
Do you think your feelings of guilt are making it harder for you to do your job or take care of yourself?

Oh, absolutely. It's... it's ruining everything. I can't even do the one thing I'm supposed to do in this life. Like I said, I'm a personal care aide, and you have to be sharp for that, you have to be completely focused to make sure the clients are okay. But I just can't keep up with my care visits safely anymore. My mind is just so consumed by all the mistakes and the guilt, I'm completely distracted. Just the other day—I think it was Thursday—my supervisor actually had to step in and stop me right in the middle of a care-plan visit. I was supposed to be updating the client's file and checking their environment, but I just froze. I was standing there in the middle of the living room, completely stuck, just paralyzed by this crushing feeling that I was doing it all wrong and failing them. I was so overwhelmed I couldn't even form a sentence to finish the visit. She had to take over and send me out of the room. It was humiliating, but... it just proved what I already knew, that I'm completely useless to them now.

And as for taking care of myself? I don't even know what that means anymore. I used to do things, you know? I used to be involved in my community. But I've completely pulled away from everything. I used to go to church, but... well, like I told you, I know God is furious with me. How can I sit in those pews and pretend everything is fine when I can feel His anger pressing down on me? I can't face Him. So I stopped going. And I used to do Zumba, which was my way of burning off stress, and I was doing some mentoring too, trying to help out younger girls... but I've dropped all of it. I've pulled away from church, Zumba, the mentoring... just everything. 

Honestly, it takes every single ounce of energy I have just to barely manage work and getting home. That's my whole existence now. I drag myself through whatever work they still let me do, making mistakes the whole time, and then I just go home and sit in my apartment and let the guilt eat me alive. There's no room for anything else in my life anymore, not taking care of myself, not hobbies, nothing. Just the mistakes.
Are you avoiding social interactions or relationships with others due to your feelings of guilt?

Yeah, like... like I was just saying a second ago, it's exactly that. I am avoiding everyone. It all ties back into what I was just telling you about pulling away from everything. When I mentioned dropping out of church and Zumba and the mentoring program... it's because of the guilt. It really is. 

Take the mentoring, for example. I was supposed to be helping these younger girls, being a role model, but how can I sit there and give them advice when I'm carrying around all this shame? I feel like a complete fraud. I know what a terrible job I'm doing, so I just stopped answering their texts. I couldn't look them in the eye. And at church, it's not just that I can feel God's anger, it's the people too. They smile and ask how my week was, and I just want to sink into the floor because I don't deserve their kindness. So I just stay away from all of them. 

And it totally spills over into my interactions at work, too, with my clients and my boss. Like I said, I can't keep up with my care visits safely anymore. That time my supervisor had to step in and stop me during the care-plan visit? When I was just too overwhelmed and stuck to even finish it? That wasn't just me messing up a task. It was me completely failing to interact with the client. I couldn't be present with another human being because the guilt was just screaming in my ears. I can't connect with people anymore. So yeah, I avoid everyone. By the time I barely manage to drag myself through work and get home, I have absolutely nothing left to give to anyone else, not even a simple conversation. I just lock my apartment door and stay by myself.
Are you having trouble completing everyday tasks because of your guilt feelings?

Yeah... yeah, it’s exactly like that. It’s like the guilt isn't just in my head anymore, it’s... it’s actually in my body. It makes everything so incredibly heavy. Everything I do has just gotten so, so slow. I mean, even the most basic, stupid things that shouldn't take any effort at all. 

Take getting ready in the morning, for example. I’ll pull my scrubs out of the closet, right? Just my regular work clothes. And I’ll sit on the edge of my bed holding the shirt, and I just... I can't put it on. I'll sit there for what feels like an hour, just staring at the fabric, thinking about how I don't deserve to wear it, how I'm just going to go in and fail those people again. It takes so much effort just to push my arms through the sleeves. Every movement feels like I'm wading through wet concrete. 

And it's not just getting dressed. It's... it's everything. Even just answering a simple question takes forever now. Someone will ask me something, and I hear the words, I really do, but my brain is so clogged up with all the mistakes and the shame that I can't form a response. It’s like the words get stuck in my throat. People at work have definitely noticed. They keep telling me I just stand there staring like I'm completely zoned out. They'll ask if I'm okay because I'll literally just stop in the middle of the hallway or in the breakroom, and I won't even realize I've stopped. They say I just look like a statue, staring into space. I try to snap out of it, but it’s like... it's like I physically can't make myself move. The guilt just paralyzes me right where I stand. So, yeah, completing everyday tasks is... it’s almost impossible when your own body won't even cooperate with you anymore.
Do you feel like you're able to enjoy or find pleasure in things you used to like, or has that been affected by your guilt?

Enjoy? I... I don't really know. I'm not sure how to answer that, to be honest with you. Pleasure just isn't... I don't even know what that word means in my life right now. It’s hard to say if the guilt is affecting my enjoyment of things because I just don't know if I would enjoy them anyway, you know? 

Like, I haven't even tried to do anything fun to find out. I mentioned the Zumba earlier, right? And the mentoring with those younger girls, and going to church. I dropped all of that. So I can't really sit here and tell you, oh, I went to Zumba and I didn't enjoy it, because I haven't even set foot in the building. I haven't given myself the chance to find out if I can still feel pleasure. I just don't know. 

My whole day, my entire existence from the minute I wake up and sit on the edge of my bed staring at my scrubs like I told you about, to the minute I lock myself back in my apartment after messing up my care visits... there's just no room for enjoyment to even be tested. I don't do anything that's supposed to be enjoyable anymore. So I can't really say if I like things or not, or if the guilt is ruining the fun, because there is no fun to ruin. I just... I really haven't noticed one way or the other. I don't have a good answer for you on that one. I just don't know.
Do you feel like you're able to find any happiness or pleasure in the things you do anymore?

I... I think I just said that, didn't I? About the pleasure and enjoying things? I'm sorry, my head is just so full of everything else, but... yeah, I really don't know how to answer that any better than I just did. Happiness just feels like a completely foreign concept right now. I don't know if I'm capable of feeling it because I don't do anything that would make me happy. 

Like I was saying about the Zumba classes and the mentoring... I used to love those things, I really did. I used to look forward to them all week. Getting the music going, seeing the girls smile when they figured something out... but I haven't done any of that in so long. I haven't even tried. So I can't say for sure if I'd feel happy doing them now, because I'm just not doing them. I'm just existing, going to work, struggling through my visits, coming home, and locking the door. There's no space in that routine for happiness to even try to sneak in. 

And even if I did try... I just keep thinking about how I don't deserve to be happy. Not after all the mistakes I've made, all the ways I'm failing my clients and everyone around me. How could I possibly sit there and enjoy a Zumba class or a cup of coffee or anything when I'm such a terrible person? It just wouldn't be right. So no, I don't feel any happiness or pleasure, but I also don't know if I could even if I tried, because I just haven't tried. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you're looking for, but it's the only one I have. I just... I really don't know anymore.
Are you having trouble taking care of your personal hygiene due to your guilt feelings?

Hygiene? Like... showering and stuff? I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed a huge change there. It's not like the guilt is specifically keeping me from brushing my teeth or anything. I don't know, it's hard to separate it all out. 

I mean, I still get in the shower. I have to, right? Because of work. I work as a personal care aide, so I'm in close contact with people all day. You can't just go in smelling bad when you're literally helping other people bathe and get dressed. The agency has rules about that. So I make myself do it. But it's like I was saying before, about getting dressed? It's the same kind of feeling. I'll stand in the shower, and the water will just be running over me, and I'll just stand there. Sometimes I don't even remember if I washed my hair or used soap because my mind is just replaying every single mistake I've ever made. Every time I was too slow to help a client, every time I didn't notice they were uncomfortable... it just loops and loops. 

So, I am doing it, I am taking care of my hygiene, but I'm not really *present* for it, if that makes sense? The guilt is there, it's always there, weighing me down, making the physical act of washing my hair feel like I'm lifting boulders. But it hasn't stopped me from actually doing it. I haven't just given up on showering or brushing my hair, at least not yet. It just takes a lot longer, and it feels like a massive chore that I don't deserve to do. Like, why should I get to feel clean and refreshed when I'm such a failure to my clients? But I do it anyway, because I have to. So, no, I don't think the guilt is stopping me from taking care of my hygiene. I just... I don't think I've noticed it being a specific problem, other than just being part of the overall heaviness of everything.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find no pleasure in due to your feelings of guilt?

I... I feel like we just talked about this, didn't we? With the Zumba and the mentoring? I'm sorry, my brain is just so foggy, but... yeah, I don't really have a different answer for you on that. Like I was trying to explain before, I haven't even tried to do any of those things I used to like. The Zumba classes, the mentoring the younger girls at the community center, going to church on Sundays... I just stopped doing all of it. 

So I can't really sit here and tell you that I went to a Zumba class and the guilt ruined it for me, or that I tried to help one of the girls with her homework and couldn't feel happy about it because I was too busy thinking about what a terrible person I am. I haven't put myself in a position to even test that out. I just wake up, stare at my scrubs, drag myself to my clients' houses, mess everything up, and then come home and lock the door. There's no room for activities in that. 

And honestly, even if I did try to go back to Zumba or church... I just don't think I deserve it. I don't deserve to have fun or feel good when I'm failing so badly at my job, when I'm letting down the people who depend on me the most. How could I justify dancing around to music when I can barely manage to help Mrs. Higgins with her breakfast without feeling like I'm doing it all wrong? It just wouldn't be right. But as far as actually trying an activity and finding no pleasure in it because of the guilt... I just haven't tried. I don't know what else to tell you. I haven't noticed it happening because I'm just not doing anything anymore.
Do you feel like you're able to experience any pleasure or enjoyment when you're engaging in activities that you used to find pleasurable?

I'm... wait, I'm sorry, but didn't you just ask me that? Like, literally just a second ago? About the activities and the pleasure? I... I feel like I'm losing my mind here, or maybe I'm just doing a really terrible job of explaining myself, which honestly wouldn't surprise me. But I really, truly don't have a different answer for you. It's exactly like I just said... I haven't been engaging in any of those things I used to find pleasurable. None of them. 

I haven't set foot in the community center. I haven't seen the girls I mentor. I haven't put on my workout clothes for Zumba. I haven't done any of it. So I can't tell you if I'm able to experience enjoyment while doing them, because I'm just not doing them at all. It's like... it's like asking me if a certain type of food tastes good when I haven't taken a single bite of it in months. I just don't know. My entire life right now is just this endless, heavy loop of waking up, putting on my scrubs, going to work, messing everything up with my clients, and then coming home and shutting the world out. That's it. That's my whole existence. 

There is absolutely no space in my day where I'm engaging in anything fun or pleasurable to even test out whether I could enjoy it or not. And like I said, I wouldn't even deserve to enjoy it if I did try, not with how much of a failure I am to people like Mrs. Higgins. So... I'm sorry, I really am, I just don't know what else you want me to say. I haven't noticed if I can feel pleasure during those activities because those activities just aren't a part of my life anymore. Am I misunderstanding what you're asking me? Because I feel like I keep giving you the exact same answer.
